datasets.name: farm_costs_2025.csv
datasets.description: 40 input-cost orders for a grain farm in 2025

questions.question: Compute the mean yield (in bu/ac) across all 50 fields.
questions.notes: Use AVERAGE on the yield_bu_ac column. Make sure you do not include the header row.

questions.question: Compute the median yield (in bu/ac) across all 50 fields.
questions.notes: MEDIAN is less sensitive to outliers than AVERAGE. Here the median is slightly higher than the mean, indicating a mild left skew.

questions.question: Compute the sample standard deviation of yield (in bu/ac) across all 50 fields.
questions.notes: Use STDEV.S (divides by n-1) for a sample. STDEV.P is only correct when you have the full population.

questions.question: Compute the 90th percentile of yield (the value below which 90% of fields lie).
questions.notes: Use PERCENTILE.INC for this course. The .EXC variant uses a slightly different interpolation.

questions.question: How many fields have a yield strictly greater than 48 bu/ac?
questions.notes: The criterion must be a string in quotes. ">48" is strict; use ">=48" for at-or-above.

questions.question: Compute the average yield of fields in the "South" region only.
questions.notes: AVERAGEIF filters rows by the criterion and averages the target range. A PivotTable would also work and lets you see all three regions at once.

questions.question: Which variety has the largest total acres planted across all 50 fields?
questions.formula: PivotTable: variety on Rows, acres in Values (Sum), sort descending
questions.notes: You could also use =SUMIF(C2:C51, "DKTC 9105", D2:D51) one variety at a time, but PivotTables are much faster for grouped summaries.

questions.question: Compute the total production (in bushels) across all 50 fields. Production = yield (bu/ac) × acres.
questions.notes: SUMPRODUCT multiplies two ranges element-wise and sums the result. Always check that units cancel: acres × (bu/ac) = bushels.

questions.question: Compute the total amount spent with "Prairie Ag Supply" across all their orders (price per unit × quantity, summed).
questions.notes: Alternative: add a helper column =E2*F2 (line total), then =SUMIF(C2:C41, "Prairie Ag Supply", G2:G41). Both work.

questions.question: What is the highest price per unit ever paid for Urea across all orders?
questions.notes: MAXIFS (Excel 2019+) is the cleanest approach. Alternative: {=MAX(IF(D2:D41="Urea", E2:E41))} as an array formula.
